version.changelog: v1.0.4: Unify naming - all references use Skill Quality Check consistently.

llm.summary: This is a markdown-only skill-quality checklist that reads skill files and produces audit scores, with no hidden execution, persistence, credential use, or destructive behavior found.

dimensions.detail: Reading local skill files and optional support files is proportionate for a skill auditor. The documented curl example is limited to fetching a user-targeted remote SKILL.md, not remote code execution.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains markdown documentation and examples only; no executable install scripts, package hooks, dependencies, or metadata-driven privilege changes were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks the agent to read target SKILL.md files and optionally fetch a GitHub raw SKILL.md with curl when the user is auditing a remote skill. That access is purpose-aligned and disclosed, though users should provide explicit targets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No instructions create background processes, persistent memory entries, scheduled tasks, tool wrappers, credential access, or self-modifying behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to audit AI Agent SKILL.md files for writing quality, trigger clarity, layering, examples, and performance impact; its instructions and bundled references consistently support that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to review other skill files for quality. When using it, point it at a specific local SKILL.md or known GitHub source, and remember that its output is a quality score rather than a security guarantee.
llm.findings:
[RA1] unexpected: Downgraded as unsupported by artifact evidence: the cited README text describes a recommended workflow involving Skill Vetter, Quality Check, and Skill Creator, not self-modification or runtime changes to this skill.
[SQP-1] expected: Partially accepted as a quality note: the main description uses broad words like audit, quality, review, and vet, but they are tied to AI Agent Skills and SKILL.md audits, so this is not a security concern by itself.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded for the example skill files: broad PDF/document triggers appear inside good/bad illustrative examples used to teach quality evaluation, not as this skill's own runtime authority.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted only as minor polish: a few Chinese phrases appear in otherwise English documentation, but they do not alter authority, hide behavior, or create a security-relevant locale constraint.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as documentation inconsistency: README examples and file structure refer to skill-audit while the skill name is skill-quality-check. This could confuse invocation but does not indicate malicious or high-impact behavior.
